note: Frozen before any Gen12.2 outcome-bearing model was fitted. Every pattern is matched against the RDKit-canonical SMILES of the extractant and against nothing else. A pattern is counted with uniquify=True, so a symmetric motif that matches in two directions over the same atom set counts once. These are motif counts over a 2D molecular graph; they are not coordination numbers and not geometry.

O_amide_carbonyl.why: amide carbonyl oxygen; the principal hard donor of every amide-type extractant in this cohort

O_ester_carbonyl.why: ester carbonyl oxygen; a weaker donor than an amide carbonyl and counted apart from it

O_carboxyl.why: carboxylic acid / carboxylate oxygens; strong anionic donors when deprotonated

O_ketone.why: carbonyl oxygen that is neither amide, ester nor carboxyl (ketone/aldehyde)

O_ether.why: aliphatic ether oxygen with two sp3-carbon neighbours: the bridging donor of a diglycolamide, a podand and a crown

O_hydroxyl.why: alcohol/phenol oxygen, excluding the acidic OH of a carboxyl (counted as O_carboxyl)

O_phosphoryl.why: phosphoryl oxygen: CMPO, phosphine oxide, phosphonate, phosphate

O_phosphate_ester.why: P-O-C ester oxygen; a weak donor, counted apart from the phosphoryl oxygen

O_nitroxide.why: N-oxide oxygen; one pyridine-N-oxide bis(phosphine oxide) is present in this cohort

N_aromatic.why: pyridine-type aromatic nitrogen with a free lone pair; pyrrole-type [nX3] is deliberately excluded because its lone pair is in the ring pi system and it does not coordinate

N_amine.why: aliphatic amine nitrogen that is not an amide, not an anilide and not charged

S_thiophosphoryl.why: P=S soft donor of the dithiophosphinate/thiophosphate family

S_thiocarbonyl.why: C=S soft donor of the thioamide family

S_thioether_thiol.why: divalent sulfur: thioether, thiol or the S of a dithiophosphinic acid

P_phosphine.why: trivalent phosphorus lone pair; recorded for completeness, expected to be rare here

O_ether_aryl.why: aryl or diaryl ether oxygen; a weaker donor than an aliphatic ether because the lone pair is conjugated into the ring, and counted apart from it for that reason

dga_unit.why: diglycolamide backbone N-C(=O)-C-O-C-C(=O)-N; the bridging carbons may be sp3 or aromatic (pyranone analogues) and the oxygen aliphatic or aromatic. Reused verbatim from lanthanide_separation.ligand_descriptors so the Gen12.2 count is the same object gen6 used to assign the diglycolamide family.

malonamide_unit.why: malonamide backbone N-C(=O)-C-C(=O)-N. Reused verbatim from lanthanide_separation.ligand_descriptors.

cmpo_unit.why: carbamoylmethylphosphine oxide: a phosphoryl and an amide oxygen two bonds apart, the classic bifunctional actinide extractant

bis_thiophosphoryl_unit.why: two P=S donors separated by a short bridge: the TWE-23/24/27/28/29/30 dithiophosphinate family

bis_thiophosphoryl_methylene.why: the tightest member of that family, P(=S)-CH2-P(=S), which is TWE-23 and TWE-24

picolinamide_arm.why: an amide carbon on a heteroaromatic carbon adjacent to a pyridine-type nitrogen: the N,O-chelating arm of picolinamides, dipicolinamides and phenanthroline diamides

aryl_amide.why: any amide on an aromatic carbon; the superset picolinamide_arm is drawn from

carboxylate_arm.why: glycinate arm of an aminopolycarboxylate (EDTA/CDTA/HEDTA type)

beta_diketone_unit.why: 1,3-dicarbonyl chelate; note that a malonamide also matches this pattern and the two counts are reported separately rather than made exclusive

thioamide_unit.why: thioamide donor group of the CAM/TAM pairs

phosphonate_ester.why: phosphonate: one P-C bond and at least one P-O-C ester

phosphate_ester.why: phosphate/phosphoric acid ester: three P-O bonds

phosphoryl_amide_extended.why: phosphoryl and amide separated by a three-atom C-X-C bridge, X = O or N: the TWE-33 to TWE-36 series. The tighter one-atom bridge is cmpo_unit.

ring_motifs.note: Ring classes are counted from the RDKit symmetrised smallest set of smallest rings, not from SMARTS, so that fused systems are counted once per ring.

classes.diazine_like_ring: aromatic 6-ring with exactly two ring nitrogens
classes.triazine_like_ring: aromatic 6-ring with three or more ring nitrogens
classes.azole_ring: aromatic 5-ring with two or more ring nitrogens (pyrazole, triazole, imidazole)
classes.crown_like_ring: ring of size 9 or more containing three or more oxygen atoms
classes.lactam_ring: non-aromatic ring containing an amide nitrogen

topology_rules.donor_graph: shortest-path distances are computed over the heavy-atom molecular graph with RDKit GetDistanceMatrix; hydrogens are implicit and never counted
topology_rules.chelate_link_why: Two potential donors separated by four bonds or fewer on the molecular graph can close a four-, five- or six-membered chelate ring on one metal centre: a donor pair d bonds apart closes a (d+2)-membered ring. Four bonds is the malonamide amide-O to amide-O separation and the P(=S)-CH2-P(=S) sulfur-to-sulfur separation, both textbook six-membered bidentate chelates; three bonds is the diglycolamide amide-O to ether-O separation, a five-membered chelate. Six-membered is the largest ring commonly quoted as chelate-stabilised, so four is the loosest defensible link. The value is fixed here from that chemistry and is not tuned: sensitivity to 3 and 5 is reported in COORDINATION_DESCRIPTOR_SPEC.md and neither is used to define MULTI_ARM.
topology_rules.donor_cluster: connected components of the graph whose nodes are the donor atoms and whose edges join two donors at graph distance <= chelate_link_distance. One component is one chelating pocket.
topology_rules.multi_arm_rule: MULTI_ARM is true when a molecule has two or more donor clusters, i.e. it presents two or more spatially separate chelating pockets. The threshold of two is the mono-topic / poly-topic boundary and is chosen from that structural semantics, before any Gen12.2 model output was read.
topology_rules.symmetry: atom symmetry orbits come from RDKit CanonicalRankAtoms(breakTies=False), which assigns equal rank to constitutionally equivalent atoms; a repeated arm is a symmetry orbit whose members are donor-cluster roots

revision_log.defect: chelate_link_distance was 3 bonds, and the justification text mis-stated the ring size that a 3-bond donor separation closes. A donor pair d bonds apart closes a (d+2)-membered chelate ring with the metal, so 3 bonds is a five-membered ring and 4 bonds is a six-membered one. At 3 bonds every malonamide (amide O to amide O is 4 bonds) and every P(=S)-CH2-P(=S) dithiophosphinate (S to S is 4 bonds) was split into two chelating pockets, although both are textbook single-pocket bidentates closing a six-membered ring.
revision_log.found: by inventorying the descriptor over all 183 cohort structures and reading the topicity of the malonamide family; no target value and no model output was consulted

revision_log.what: chelate_link_distance raised to 4 bonds, so that four-, five- and six-membered chelate rings all count as one pocket; ether oxygen split into aliphatic and aryl classes; the phosphoryl+amide motif that failed to match the TWE-33..36 series replaced by one with the correct bridge length
revision_log.found: structure-only, before any Gen12.2 level target was computed and before any model was fitted
